However, some studies have suggested that long-term therapy with epo- prostenol may also have a role as an alternative to trans- plantation. Sustained clinical improvement and improved survival have been reported15,16 in some patients given long-term intravenous therapy using portable infusion pumps, and guidelines1,9,10 now recommend that epopros- tenol may be used in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension who do not respond to calcium-channel blockers and who are in functional class III or class IV. Continuous intravenous iloprost, a more stable analogue, has also shown some benefit,17 and may be an alternative. Another analogue, treprostinil, can be given by continuous subcutaneous infusion18,19 and may be used, particularly in patients for whom intravenous treatment is not suitable;10 a small study20 has reported the safe transfer of patients from epoprostenol to treprostinil therapy. However, severe pain may occur with subcutaneous treprostinil, and it may be given intravenously if required.10,21 Prostaglandin ana- logues have also been given by inhalation. Epoprostenol has been used, but iloprost, which has a longer action, is generally preferred;10,22 treprostinil has also been used.23 Another analogue, beraprost sodium, has been given oral- ly,24-26 but is not widely available. Although primarily thought to act as vasodilators, epoprostenol and its ana- logues also affect vascular remodelling and platelet aggre- gation and this may contribute to their beneficial effects. Endothelin receptor antagonists may also be used. Endo- thelin-1 is a potent endogenous vasoconstrictor and ap- pears to be overproduced in pulmonary arterial hyperten- sion; it also stimulates vascular remodelling and has pro- inflammatory effects. Bosentan, an oral endothelin recep- tor antagonist, has been shown27,28 to improve haemody- namics and exercise capacity, and there is some evidence that survival may also be improved.29 It may be used as an alternative to prostacyclin analogues in patients in func- tional class III and a small study30 has suggested that some patients can be safely transferred from prostacyclin ana- logues to bosentan. However, in unstable functional class IV patients, epoprostenol is usually preferred.1,10 Studies with sitaxentan31 and ambrisentan,32 which are selective for the endothelin ETA-receptor, have also demonstrated positive results.
